title: Welcome
description: A Discord bot for labels, collectives, and A&R teams
text: Vektra is a Discord bot built for music labels, collectives, and A&R teams who need a clean way to collect demos, review submissions, manage staff notes, and stay in touch with artists - all from inside Discord. Pro servers can also use the Vektra dashboard to review submissions, manage tickets, submit release requests, edit branding, change storage, post panels, and view analytics from the web. Pro+ servers can host a white-label bot identity from the dashboard. Free is $0 forever. Paid plans start at $3.99 — see Plans & Pricing /free-vs-pro for what each tier includes and how to buy. How it works Artists submit demos through a Discord form. Your staff receives a private submission card with Approve , Reject , and DM buttons. Each submission can open a private staff thread where decisions, notes, DMs, and release logs stay attached to the right ticket. Servers can also use Vektra as a private support-ticket tool - users click a public ticket button, and the actual ticket appears in a staff-only channel. Server admins can also submit release requests for Vektra QC before Labelcaster delivery. Set up Vektra in your server in a few minutes. How artists submit demos and track their submissions. Review, approve, reject, and DM artists from Discord or the dashboard. See what's included in each plan. Run a private ticket flow for your community Pro . Manage submissions, tickets, releases, and settings from the web. Full reference of every slash command. Host a white-label bot identity for your label.

title: Getting started
description: Add Vektra to your Discord server and set it up in a few minutes
text: This guide walks server admins through adding Vektra and getting it ready to receive demos. Before you start You need to be an admin, or have Manage Server permissions, in the Discord server where you want to install Vektra. Vektra also needs permission to send messages, create threads, and send DMs to users who interact with it. Invite Vektra Setup steps Invite Vektra to your Discord server using the invite link. When prompted, accept the default permissions so the bot can read channels, send messages, and create threads. In your server, run: Replace Label Name with your label or collective's name. This creates managed storage for your server and sets your label name, which Vektra uses across messages and embeds. Free and Starter servers are automatically assigned managed storage. Pro and Pro+ servers can choose a storage region or connect their own Neon database. See Plans /free-vs-pro . Choose where staff-only submission cards should appear: Pick a private channel that only your reviewers can see. This is where incoming demo cards with Approve, Reject, and DM buttons will appear. Pro and Pro+ servers can run private support tickets. Tickets need their own staff channel: This channel must be different from your demo submission staff channel. Run: Vektra confirms your storage, premium status, branding, staff channel, ticket channel, and thread permissions. You can also use: - /db status to check storage connection - /staff status to check staff channel connection Artists run /submit anywhere in your server to open the demo submission form. Pin a message or post in your submissions channel so artists know what to do. Dashboard setup Pro and Pro+ servers can manage Vektra from the web dashboard. 1. Log in with Discord. 2. Choose a server from the custom server picker. 3. Confirm Vektra is installed and that you have Admin or Manage Server permission. 4. Edit branding, templates, ticket settings, storage, release requests, and panel posting from the dashboard. The dashboard only shows servers you can manage and where Vektra is installed. Dashboard review tools require an active Pro or Pro+ tier. When posting panels from the dashboard, the channel list comes from channels visible to the bot. If a panel fails to post, check that Vektra can view the channel and send messages there. Pro+ white-label setup Pro+ servers also get a Pro+ Bot page in the dashboard. Use it after the normal server setup is complete: 1. Create a Discord application and bot in the Discord Developer Portal. 2. Copy the bot client ID and raw bot token. 3. Open Dashboard - Pro+ Bot . 4. Paste the client ID and token. 5. Choose the hosted bot status. 6. Enable the hosted bot and save. 7. Invite the custom bot to the same server. The hosted custom bot is locked to the configured Pro+ server. If it is invited to a different server, it leaves automatically. In Discord: To check releases submitted by this server: Dashboard users on Pro and Pro+ can also submit release requests from the Releases page. The dashboard form uses separate metadata fields, so it does not need the AI metadata check used by the Discord modal. Recommended channel setup - A public channel where artists can learn how to submit. - A private staff channel for demo cards. - A private staff ticket channel if you use Pro support tickets. - Optional approved and rejected routing channels for Starter, Pro, or Pro+ servers. title: Artist Guide
description: How to submit demos and track your submissions
text: If you're an artist sending demos to a label that uses Vektra, everything happens inside Discord. No external links, no sign-ups. Submitting a demo In the label's Discord server, run: A form opens with up to five fields. Starter, Pro, and Pro+ labels can customize the optional message prompt with their own question. Fill it in and submit - you'll get a confirmation with your ticket ID . Keep this if you want to check on the submission later. Always submit your strongest work. Most labels keep a public leaderboard of top accepted submitters via /leaderboard . Tracking your submissions Command What it does --- --- /submission ticket id: Look up one submission by its ticket ID you can only see your own /my subs Show your submissions in the current server /my demos Show a longer list of demos you submitted /my stats Show your total submitted, accepted, rejected, and queued counts /leaderboard Show the top accepted submitters in this server The leaderboard groups by Discord user, not by display name, so changing your nickname won't split your stats. Replying to staff If the label's staff sends you a DM through the bot , you can reply directly to that DM message. Your reply, including attachments, is automatically forwarded back to the staff thread for your submission or support ticket. Attachments you send are reuploaded into the staff thread so they remain available after Discord's original DM attachment link expires. Very large files may still appear as temporary links if Discord will not let the bot reupload them. Tips - Submit one track per /submit . - If the server has a cooldown, duplicate-link rule, or per-user submission cap, the bot will let you know. - Make sure your DMs are open to server members so staff can reach you.

title: Staff Workflow
description: Review, approve, reject, and DM artists from Discord
text: Vektra gives staff a structured way to handle incoming demos without leaving Discord. Pro and Pro+ teams can also review from the Vektra dashboard. Dashboard decisions update the database, DM the artist when approving or rejecting, and update the original staff card when the submission has Discord message references stored. See the Dashboard guide /dashboard for the full web workflow. How submissions appear When an artist runs /submit , a submission card is posted to your staff channel. Each card includes: - The artist's submitted info - Buttons for Approve , Reject , and DM - Pro quick-status buttons for common label workflow steps - A private staff discussion thread for that submission The staff thread is where your team keeps notes, release logs, and any back-and-forth with the artist. Browsing submissions Command What it does --- --- /queue Newest submissions still in queue /recent Newest submissions across all statuses /panel Admin browser with filters, pages, and refresh controls /status ticket id: new status: Update a submission's status Reviewing from the dashboard The dashboard is useful when staff wants a larger view of submissions, analytics, and tickets. - Approve or reject submissions from the web. - Send DMs to the submitter from a submission. - Export submission data as CSV. - Filter recent submissions and view analytics graphs. When a dashboard approval or rejection is sent, the artist receives the same kind of DM they would receive from Discord buttons. For new submissions, Vektra also updates the original staff card in Discord so the decision buttons are no longer active. Older submissions created before staff-card references were stored may still show old Discord buttons, even though the database status is already updated. Submission statuses - In Queue : not yet reviewed - Needs Review : flagged for a second listen - Shortlisted : on the shortlist - Processed : reviewed and handled internally - Contacted : staff has reached out to the artist - Signed : artist signed - Approved : demo accepted - Rejected : demo declined Actions on a submission card Marks the submission as accepted. If you've set up approval routing with /routing Starter , it is automatically posted to your approved channel. The artist gets the configured approval DM Starter: customize with /templates . Dashboard approvals behave the same way. Marks the submission as rejected. Pro servers can use saved rejection reasons /reasons , while Starter and above can customize rejection DM templates /templates . Dashboard rejections also DM the artist. Opens a DM to the artist directly from the bot. When the artist replies to that DM, their message and attachments are forwarded back into the matching staff thread. The DM button stays available after a submission is approved, rejected, or moved to another status. Pro submission cards include quick buttons for Review, Shortlist, Processed, Contacted, and Signed. These update the submission status without sending an approval or rejection DM. Keeping release logs Use the staff thread attached to each submission to log: - Decisions and reasoning - Mastering or release dates - Contracts sent - Anything else tied to that artist or track Because the thread is linked to the submission, you can always find this history later. Release requests Release requests are separate from demo submissions. They are for labels that want Vektra QC before Labelcaster delivery. Server admins can submit a release request: Admins can check the status of release requests submitted by the current server: Each release request stores its accepted or rejected status and decision reason. Accepted and rejected updates can also be sent to the submitter by DM from the owner review flow. /make-release and /check-releases are admin-only commands. title: Support Tickets
description: Run private support tickets from Discord
text: Support tickets are a Pro feature for labels that want a private help desk inside Discord. The public side is simple: users click a button and fill out a short form. The staff side stays private in the channel you choose. Support tickets require their own private staff channel. This must be different from the demo submission staff channel set with /setup staff . How tickets work 1. Staff chooses a private ticket channel. 2. Staff posts a public ticket panel. 3. A user clicks Open Ticket and fills out the form. 4. Vektra posts the ticket card in the private staff channel. 5. Staff can resolve the ticket or DM the user from the card. The submitter cannot see the staff ticket card or staff discussion thread. They only receive a confirmation that the ticket was opened. Pro and Pro+ staff can also review tickets from the dashboard, change ticket status, and DM the user from the ticket detail view. Setup Set the private staff ticket channel: Post the public ticket panel: Users click the button on that panel to open tickets. Use a staff-only channel for /ticket channel and a public or community-facing channel for /ticket panel . Do not use the same staff channel that receives demo submissions. Staff actions Ticket cards include: - Resolved : marks the ticket as resolved. - DM : sends a message to the user through Vektra. When staff uses the DM button, the user's direct reply to that bot message is forwarded back into the matching ticket thread. The DM button stays available after a ticket is resolved. Attachments in user replies are reuploaded into the matching staff thread when they fit Discord's upload limit. Oversized files fall back to temporary Discord links. Dashboard review In the dashboard, tickets appear separately from demo submissions so staff can keep support work out of the A&R queue. - Change ticket status to Open, Waiting, Answered, or Resolved. - DM the ticket opener from the web. - Keep the private staff channel as the source of truth for the ticket card and thread. The user never sees the private staff card. Replies still route back through the bot when they reply directly to the bot's DM. Ticket commands Command Description --- --- /ticket channel channel: Set the private staff channel where ticket cards appear. /ticket panel channel: Post the public button panel users click to open tickets. /tickets status: List recent support tickets. /ticket set ticket id: new status: Update a support ticket status. Available ticket statuses: - Open - Waiting - Answered - Resolved Best practices - Keep the staff ticket channel private. - Use the DM button instead of manually messaging users, so replies return to the correct thread. - Resolve tickets when the issue is finished. - Use clear subject lines so staff can scan tickets quickly.

title: Dashboard
description: Manage submissions, tickets, releases, branding, storage, and analytics from the web
text: The Vektra dashboard is the web control surface for Pro and Pro+ servers. It uses Discord login, then shows the servers where you can manage Vektra. Dashboard access requires Discord OAuth, Vektra installed in the server, and an active Pro or Pro+ tier. The server picker only shows servers you can manage. What the dashboard can do Area What it does --- --- Overview Shows recent activity, demo counts, open ticket counts, and daily charts. Submissions Review demos, update status, approve, reject, DM artists, and open track links. Tickets Review support tickets, change ticket status, resolve tickets, and DM users. Releases Submit releases for Vektra QC and track accepted or rejected release status. Analytics View submission and decision trends with line charts and staff workload data. Branding Edit display name, submit panel caption, embed color, tutorial panel templates, footer, and logo. Messages Post custom embeds or plain messages to any channel the bot can access. Settings Change demo intake, storage, staff channels, templates, ticket channels, and post panels. Pro+ Bot Configure hosted white-label bot identity for Pro+ servers. Developer API keys, custom sender domains, email templates, and the AI/MCP connector. Login and server access 1. Open the dashboard at vektra.games 2. Log in with Discord. 3. Pick a server from the server dropdown. The dashboard checks your Discord permissions. You need to be the server owner, an admin, or have Manage Server permission to see the server in the dashboard. Some release actions are stricter. Submitting release requests from the dashboard requires server admin access, matching the /make-release Discord command. Reviewing submissions From the Submissions page, staff can: - Change a demo's status. - Open a review form with rating, reviewer, shortlist, priority, decision reason, and staff notes. - Approve or reject a submission. - DM the artist from the dashboard. - Open the submitted demo link. When a dashboard approval or rejection is saved, Vektra can DM the artist and update the original Discord staff card if the submission has stored message references. Very old submissions created before Discord message references were stored may update in the database without disabling the old Discord buttons. Reviewing tickets The Tickets page keeps support work separate from the demo queue. - Move tickets between Open, Waiting, Answered, and Resolved. - Send a DM reply to the ticket opener. - Keep the private Discord ticket channel as the staff record. User replies still route back through Vektra when the user replies directly to the bot's DM message. Release requests Release requests are for labels that want Vektra QC before Labelcaster delivery. From Discord, admins can use: From the dashboard, server admins can use the Releases page to submit a release with separate fields instead of a single AI-parsed paragraph. Dashboard release submissions do not use SambaNova metadata checks because the form asks for the required metadata directly. Required release fields: - Label name - Album title - Artists - Label owner legal name - Email IDs for every artist and the label owner, clearly mapped to each person - C line - P line - Composers and producers legal names - Drive or downloadable file link Optional fields can be left blank and treated as Auto: - UPC code - Number of tracks - Version titles or names - Track titles - Release date - Genre - Explicit content - ISRCs The release appears in the configured Vektra QC channel with a private discussion thread. Accepted or rejected status, decision notes, and rejection reasons are shown back in the dashboard and through /check-releases . Distribution fee Free servers can submit release requests, but Vektra takes a 10% service fee on distribution handled through Vektra. The label keeps 90% . Paid tiers keep 100% of distribution earnings. Accepting or rejecting releases The Vektra owner review workspace can accept or reject release requests from the dashboard.

title: Pro+
description: White-label bot hosting for labels that want their own Discord bot identity
text: Pro+ includes everything in Pro plus white-label bot hosting . A Pro+ server can connect its own Discord bot application so artists and staff interact with that label's own bot identity instead of only the shared Vektra bot. Pro+ white-label hosting is self-serve from the dashboard. The server still uses Vektra's workflow, storage, commands, panels, and dashboard, but the hosted bot can use the buyer's own Discord bot token and status. Included features Pro+ includes everything from Pro: - Starter branding and customization - Pro A&R workflow tools - Pro storage options - Pro dashboard access - Pro support tickets - Pro analytics and exports - Release requests and dashboard release tracking It also adds: - A dedicated hosted Discord bot worker for that server - Custom bot token supplied by the buyer - Custom bot online status from the dashboard - A custom invite link based on the buyer's bot client ID - Dashboard restart requests for the hosted worker - Discord-side hosting controls with /white label and /white label status - Automatic shutdown when Pro+ expires or the hosted bot is disabled What the buyer needs The buyer creates a Discord application in the Discord Developer Portal and provides: - Bot token - Bot client ID - Desired status type and status text The bot name, avatar, and profile description are managed in the buyer's Discord Developer Portal. Vektra hosts the bot connection and workflow. A Discord bot token is like a password. Only paste tokens from Discord applications you own. If a token is exposed, reset it in the Discord Developer Portal and update it in the dashboard. Dashboard setup 1. Buy or redeem Pro+ at vektra.games/pricing $16.99/month . 2. Open vektra.games and log in with Discord. 3. Choose the Pro+ server. 4. Open Pro+ Bot . 5. Paste the custom bot client ID and token. 6. Choose the status type and status text. 7. Enable the hosted bot and save. 8. Use the status presets or Restart hosted bot when changing runtime behavior. 9. Use Invite custom bot to add that bot to the same server. The VPS manager checks for changes roughly every 30 seconds. The dashboard will show manager status such as pending restart , starting , online , stopped , or error . Discord controls Pro+ admins can manage the hosted worker from Discord too: Command What it does --- --- /white label status Shows enabled state, token presence, worker status, last seen time, and the invite link. /white label enabled: Starts or pauses the hosted worker. /white label enabled: status type: status text: Updates the hosted bot status and queues a manager restart. Token and client ID setup stays in the dashboard so sensitive token entry only happens in one place. Server lock Discord's invite screen may let someone choose any server where they have permission to add bots. Vektra still locks each white-label worker to the configured Pro+ server. If the custom bot is invited to the wrong server, it leaves automatically. On startup, it also checks existing guilds and leaves any server that does not match the configured Pro+ server. Expiry and removal When Pro+ expires, the white-label worker stops automatically on the next manager check. The stored configuration remains in the dashboard so it can be reused after renewal. To remove or stop a custom bot: - Disable it from Dashboard - Pro+ Bot . - Or remove premium with the owner-side premium controls. - Or stop the Pro+ manager service if all hosted custom bots need to be paused. Current hosting limit Vektra currently runs Pro+ hosting as a controlled beta. The default manager limit is 5 active white-label bots on the VPS. This limit keeps memory usage predictable. It can be adjusted later when hosting capacity increases. How is this different from Pro branding? title: Commands
description: Full reference of public Vektra slash commands
text: Every public Vektra slash command, grouped by who uses it. Run /help in Discord to see a shorter command list inside your server. Commands marked Starter require Starter, Pro, or Pro+. Commands marked Pro require Pro or Pro+. Paid commands are synced per server, so lower-tier servers usually will not see commands they cannot use. Bot-owner-only maintenance commands are intentionally not listed here. Everyone Command Description --- --- /help Show the command list and setup steps inside Discord. /invite Show a clickable invite link for adding Vektra to another server. /premium See how to buy Starter, Pro, or Pro+ — or open vektra.games/pricing /pro status Check whether the current server has an active premium tier. Artists Command Description --- --- /submit Open the demo submission form. /submission ticket id: Look up one submission. Artists can only view their own submissions; staff can view any submission. /my subs Show your submissions in the current server. /my demos Show a longer list of demos you submitted. /my stats Show your submitted, accepted, rejected, and queued counts. /leaderboard Show top accepted submitters, grouped by Discord user so name changes do not split stats. Server Setup Command Description --- --- /start label name: Create managed Vektra storage and set the server's label name. /setup staff channel: Set the private staff channel where new submission cards are posted. /setup Check storage, Pro status, branding, staff channel, ticket channel, demo intake, and thread permissions. /intake open: message: Admin: open or close demo submissions for the server. Works on every tier. /open submissions Admin: open demo submissions. Works on every tier. /close submissions message: Admin: close demo submissions and optionally set the message artists see. Works on every tier. /db status Check which storage is connected. Free and Starter servers use managed storage automatically. Pro and Pro+ servers can move regions or connect a custom database. When storage changes, Vektra migrates existing submissions, tickets, branding, and Pro settings before switching. Pro and Pro+ servers can also edit storage, branding, templates, routing, ticket settings, and panel posting from the dashboard. Staff Submissions Command Description --- --- /queue Show the newest submissions still in queue. /recent Show the newest submissions across all statuses. /panel Open an admin browser with filters, pages, and refresh controls. /status ticket id: new status: Update a submission's status. Available submission statuses: - In Queue - Needs Review - Shortlisted - Processed - Contacted - Signed - Approved - Rejected Staff submission cards also include Approve , Reject , and DM buttons. DM reply forwarding works when the artist replies directly to the bot's DM message. Attachments are reuploaded into the staff thread when they fit Discord's upload limit; oversized files fall back to temporary Discord links. title: Developer API
text: Vektra API Documentation Welcome to the Vektra Developer API — the official API for receiving and managing demo submissions, support tickets, releases, and email automation through your own website, app, or AI assistant. --- Base URL --- Authentication All API requests must include your API key in the request headers. Or as a Bearer token: Generate your API key from the Dashboard → Developer → API Keys tab. Scoping Vektra issues two kinds of keys: Key type What it can access --- --- Workspace key Everything in the label: submissions, analytics, tickets, releases, webhooks, and email settings. Person key Bound to one artist's email — only that person's own submissions, analytics, and tickets. Cannot read or change webhooks, releases, or email settings. Use person keys when handing an artist or their AI assistant access to their own data. --- Endpoints GET /v1/submissions Fetch demo submissions from your label's database. title: MCP & AI Assistants
description: Connect Claude and other AI tools to your Vektra workspace through the hosted MCP connector
text: Vektra ships a hosted MCP connector that lets AI assistants like Claude read and manage your workspace directly — list submissions, review tickets, update email templates, and more — without any local setup. What is MCP? MCP Model Context Protocol is the standard way AI assistants connect to external tools. Vektra exposes its public API as MCP tools over a hosted endpoint, so an assistant can act on your label's data with your permission. Everything runs from the Dashboard deployment — no extra server to host, no local process. Connecting Claude one click The connector uses OAuth with Discord , so staff can sign in without copying keys around. 1. Open Claude Desktop, claude.ai, or Cowork and add a custom connector. 2. Enter the connector URL: 3. Sign in with Discord and pick the workspace server you manage. 4. The connector appears with Vektra's tools ready to use. Connecting with an API key Prefer a plain key? Use the same URL with bearer-token auth: Generate the key in Dashboard → Developer → API Keys . A workspace key unlocks every tool; a person key is scoped to one artist's own submissions, analytics, and tickets. Available tools Tool What it does --- --- list submissions List demo submissions, newest first. create submission Submit a demo on behalf of an artist. delete submission Permanently delete a submission by ID. get analytics Status/rating breakdowns, activity, top artists. list releases List release packages queued for QC. list tickets List support tickets. create ticket Open a support ticket. delete ticket Permanently delete a ticket by ID. list webhooks List webhook subscriptions and delivery status. subscribe webhook Subscribe a URL to workspace events. unsubscribe webhook Remove a webhook subscription. get email settings Read the workspace email template, reply address, and Resend status. update email template Set the custom HTML email template and/or reply address. get api guide Return the full public API reference. get mailing guide Explain how artist emailing works Resend, reply links, placeholders . Scoping and security - Every MCP request is authenticated with your bearer token — the same credential the tools use to call the API, so a connection can only see what its key is allowed to see. - Workspace keys see the whole label; person keys only see the bound person's data. Workspace-level tools webhooks, releases, email settings are rejected for person keys. - The OAuth flow binds the connection to the logged-in user's chosen label with the same scoping rules. - Connections are stateless — nothing is installed on your machine and no local process is needed. OAuth details for advanced setups The connector is a standard MCP streamable-HTTP server with RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata: Clients that support OAuth discovery Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Cowork use it automatically. Everything else can authenticate with a bearer API key. See also - Developer API /api — the full HTTP API reference these tools are built on. - Email & artist notifications /email — how artist emails, reply links, and templates work.

title: Email & Artist Notifications
description: How Vektra emails artists: Resend setup, custom sender domains, templates, and one-time reply links
text: Vektra can email artists status updates on their demos, with branded templates and secure one-time reply links. Everything is configured from the Dashboard → Developer tab. How mailing works Artist emails are sent through Resend . Each workspace stores its own Resend API key, sender domain, reply address, and optional custom HTML template. When a submission's status changes Approved / Rejected / In Queue : 1. Vektra first tries to DM the artist on Discord if they're in your server. 2. If they aren't in the server, Vektra sends a branded email with the new status, the submission ID, track title, and any message from your A&R team. 3. Every status email includes a one-time reply link — the artist clicks it, writes back, and Vektra forwards the reply to your staff Discord thread. Setting it up 1. Open Dashboard → Developer . 2. Add a Resend API key in the "Sender Email & Resend API" section. 3. Add a custom sender domain e.g. demos.yourlabel.com and verify it with Resend — emails are sent from "Your Label" . 4. Set a reply-to address if you want replies to go somewhere specific. Without a Resend key, emails cannot be sent — the Developer tab and GET /v1/settings/email reports resend key set: false . Custom sender domain Use your own domain so emails come from your label, not a Vektra address: 1. Add a CNAME record at your DNS provider pointing to Vektra. 2. Enter the domain in Dashboard → Developer → Custom Domain . 3. Verify the DNS records with Resend from the same screen. Once verified, emails are sent from demos@yourdomain.com . A default yourlabel.vektra.games address is always available if you don't set a custom domain. Custom email templates You can supply your own HTML template — write it in the Developer → Email Template editor, or let an AI assistant do it through the MCP connector /mcp update email template . When a template is set, every artist email is rendered from it; when it's empty, Vektra's built-in template is used. Allowed placeholders: Placeholder Replaced with --- --- {label name} Your label's name {subject} The email subject {artist name} The artist's name {headline} A short headline line {accent color} The status color green / red / amber {status} The new submission status {submission id} The submission ticket ID {track title} The track title {message} The A&R team's message text {reply url} The one-time reply link URL {reply button} The reply button label {year} The current year Rules to follow: - {reply button} is only the button text — wrap it yourself: {reply button} . - Keep the template fully self-contained with inline CSS on every element — email clients strip blocks. - Don't invent placeholders beyond the ones listed. Reply links - Every status email includes a reply link valid for 72 hours , single use. - Clicking it opens a reply page where the artist writes back. - The reply is stored and your staff Discord thread is notified so your team can follow up. Troubleshooting Symptom Cause --- --- Emails not sending, resend key set: false No Resend API key configured in Developer tab or env not loaded on the deployed server — redeploy after changing env . "Could not reach the artist" The submission has no email stored e.g. submitted via Discord without a contact email . Emails show Vektra's default sender Custom sender domain not added or DNS not verified yet. Template changes not visible Make sure you save in the Developer tab or via the API and redeploy isn't needed — the template is stored per-workspace in the database. Artist never got the email They may be in your Discord server then Vektra DMs instead of emailing , or their email was missing at submission time. See also - Developer API /api — GET / PUT /v1/settings/email and the email notification flow. - MCP & AI Assistants /mcp — have an AI assistant read or edit your email template.
